metaData.title: Cascadia Nurses Association learning programme check in

sentences.text: Afternoon. We have forty minutes and I would like to use most of it on the continuing education programme.
Afternoon. That suits me, the autumn term opened a fortnight ago so it is all very fresh.
How did the opening go? Last year you had a rush on the first morning that caused some trouble.
Much better this year. We staggered the enrolment across three days by speciality and nothing fell over.
Two thousand one hundred nurses enrolled in at least one course, which is up on last autumn by roughly nine percent.
That is a healthy number. Which courses are carrying it?
The pharmacology refresher, as always, and a new one on paediatric assessment that we were not sure about.
The paediatric one filled in two days and we have opened a second cohort for January.
Good problem to have. How are the live sessions being scheduled this term?
That is the first thing on my list, actually, and it is the one that costs us the most in small ways.
None of the session dates land in a learner's own calendar, so we paste them into a reminder note and trust people to copy them across themselves.
A nurse on shift work cannot hold four session dates in her head across a twelve week term, and we would not expect her to.
Attendance at the second and third session of a series is always about a fifth lower than the first, and I am fairly sure that is why.
Let me make sure I have the shape of it. You want the dates to reach the learner's own calendar rather than a list in an email.
Yes, and to update themselves if we move a session, which we do two or three times a term.
When we move one now we send a second email and a good number of people never see it.
Understood. That is a clean requirement and I will take it forward in your words.
The second thing is the one I have raised before, so I will say it once and then stop.
Completion still does not reach the member record on its own, so our registrar keys the finished hours in every Friday afternoon.
It is about three hours a week for her and it is three hours of copying numbers from one screen to another.
She has never once got one wrong, which I mention because the day she does we will not notice for a month.
I have that on the account already and I will add this week's figure to it.
Three hours a week is a more useful number than the general complaint, so thank you for putting it that way.
It is the number the board understands. Anything I can put in hours tends to get listened to.
Last thing from me. The accreditation renewal was due this autumn, was it not?
Submitted in August and we heard back three weeks ago. Four years rather than the two we had before.
The reviewers commented on how quickly we produced the attendance evidence, which I found quietly funny given how it is produced.
Then I have two items to write up, the calendar one and this week's number on the registrar's time.
Anything else before we finish?
Nothing else today. Thank you for the time.
